By further systematically training and evaluating a broad panel of model variants spanning model capacity, training duration and dataset size, we uncover distinct scaling behaviors across structural, evolutionary and functional capabilities. Together, these findings establish LIMBER as a versatile RNA foundation model and provide broader insights into how architectural design, internal representations and scaling shape the learning of RNA sequence-structure-function relationships.

items.title: Disease-Targeted Therapies and eGFR Slope over 2 Years in IgA Nephropathy: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Several disease-targeted therapies for IgA nephropathy have reported effects on eGFR slope over 2 years or longer in phase 3 trials, but they have not been compared directly. We compared their effects on the annualized total eGFR slope. Methods: We searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and ClinicalTrials.gov from January 2018 and reviewed nephrology congress abstracts. Randomized trials reporting the annualized eGFR slope over at least 96 weeks were eligible. Placebo-controlled trials were combined in a frequentist network meta-analysis. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in total eGFR slope; secondary outcomes included the relative reduction in eGFR slope, chronic slope, proteinuria, and safety. Results: Of 1523 records screened, six placebo-controlled trials (2437 participants) were included in the main analysis. Compared with placebo, the difference in total eGFR slope was 5.1 (95% confidence interval [CI], 3.5 to 6.7) ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year for telitacicept, 5.0 (3.6 to 6.5) for atacicept, 4.7 (3.8 to 5.6) for sibeprenlimab, 3.0 (2.0 to 4.0) for iptacopan, 1.8 (0.5 to 3.1) for targeted-release budesonide, and 1.4 (0.5 to 2.3) for atrasentan. The pooled effect of the three agents targeting a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) or B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and APRIL was 4.8 (4.2 to 5.5), and their pooled reduction relative to the control-arm decline was 98% (82% to 113%) versus 34% to 49% for the other agents. Serious adverse events were less frequent with telitacicept and atacicept than with placebo, serious infections were more frequent with iptacopan, and discontinuations were more frequent with targeted-release budesonide. Conclusions: In indirect comparisons, agents targeting APRIL or BAFF/APRIL may provide greater improvements in total eGFR slope over approximately 2 years than the other disease- targeted therapies. One of the three B-cell-directed trials was available only as a conference presentation, and direct comparisons are lacking.

items.title: Adaptive and maladaptive microstructural remodelling of the maternal brain revealed by diffusion kurtosis imaging
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Postpartum depression (PPD) is a major maternal mental health concern that may arise during neurobiological and emotional adaptation. Alterations in these adaptive processes may contribute to depressive symptom vulnerability; however, the neurobiological basis of postpartum brain adaptation remains unclear. We investigated microstructural brain remodelling in postpartum women using diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) and evaluated its association with Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) scores. We compared brain magnetic resonance imaging findings between 15 women one month postpartum and 10 nulliparous women without psychiatric disorders. Tract-based spatial statistics and regions of interest were analysed using diffusion tensor and kurtosis metrics. Compared with nulliparous women, postpartum women showed significantly lower mean and axial diffusivity values in white matter regions, including the frontal lobe, basal ganglia, and corticospinal tract. The posterior insular cortex showed increased mean and radial kurtosis, whereas the putamen demonstrated decreased diffusivity. EPDS scores showed positive correlations with kurtosis metrics in the amygdala and negative correlations with diffusivity metrics in the hypothalamus. These findings suggest that the postpartum brain undergoes coordinated microstructural remodelling involving emotional regulation, stress response, and maternal behavioural adaptations. Thus, DKI may provide an objective neuroimaging biomarker for identifying maladaptive postpartum brain changes associated with depressive symptoms.

items.title: Pharmacogenomics in Cancer Treatment: Challenges and Opportunities in African Settings.
items.abstract_or_text: Background Cancer incidence in Africa is projected to reach 2.1 million new cases annually by 2040. Current treatment guidelines remain largely based on pharmacogenomic data predominantly from European and Asian genetic profiles, potentially compromising safety and efficacy in African patients. However, limited clinical validation data, extreme intra-population genetic diversity, and significant healthcare infrastructure barriers constrain the translational application of pharmacogenomics in Africa. Objective This review critically examines pharmacogenomic variants with established clinical actionability in cancer treatment, focusing on those with differential frequencies or African-specific alleles, and evaluates the evidence base for their implementation in African healthcare settings. Methods We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, PharmGKB, dbSNP, and Google Scholar for peer-reviewed studies reporting pharmacogenomic variants in African or African-ancestry populations relevant to cancer therapeutics. We synthesised evidence from recent African and global studies on pharmacogenomic variants affecting commonly used chemotherapy agents. Results Several variants show marked frequency differences between African-ancestry reference populations and European populations, including DPYD rs115232898 (2.06% vs. 0.00%), CYP2D6*17 (18.76% vs. 0%), and CYP3A5*6 (12.82% vs. 0%). However, many of these estimates derive primarily from African-American datasets and should not be interpreted as representative of continental African populations. African-specific variants such as CYP2D6*17 and DPYD rs115232898 are underrepresented in guideline development datasets. Intra-African genetic diversity is the highest globally, with Khoi-San populations harbouring extensive private variation, suggesting that no single pharmacogenomic panel will be universally applicable across the continent. Conclusion While pharmacogenomics holds substantial promise for personalising cancer treatment in Africa, its current translational readiness is limited by a critical lack of African-specific clinical validation data. Priorities include multi-site validation studies, development of African-enriched genotyping panels, and integration of pharmacogenomic education into oncology practice. Implementation must be accompanied by ethical frameworks ensuring data sovereignty and equitable benefit-sharing.

items.title: Design, Synthesis and Biophysical Characterisation of CPP-PNA Conjugates for Targeting Oncogenic microRNA-221.
items.abstract_or_text: Peptide nucleic acids (PNAs) are a promising platform targeting disease-associated microRNAs due to their high binding affinity, excellent sequence specificity and resistance to enzymatic degradation. However, their therapeutic application is often limited by inefficient cellular uptake. In this study, we present the design, synthesis and physicochemical characterisation of cell-penetrating peptide (CPP)-PNA conjugates that target the oncogenic microRNA miRNA-221-5p, as well as their preliminary biological evaluation. Anti-miRNA-221-5p PNAs functionalised for conjugation with CPPs via Cu(I)-catalysed azide-alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) or disulfide-mediated coupling were synthesised using solid-phase peptide synthesis. Circular dichroism and UV-melting analyses confirmed the formation of a stable, sequence-specific PNA-RNA heteroduplex with miRNA-221-5p. This demonstrated strong hybridisation and high thermodynamic stability compared to scrambled control sequences. Cell proliferation assays indicated modest but reproducible antiproliferative effects for the CPP-PNA conjugates co-incubated with chloroquine, with no evidence of acute cytotoxicity. These findings emphasise the potential of CPP-PNA systems for the intracellular delivery of antisense agents and highlight the importance of the linker nature in determining their biological performance.

items.title: Machine Learning and Structural Analysis for Generation-Wise Selection of Perylene Diimide Dendrimers Based on Topological Compatibility With Drug Molecules.
items.abstract_or_text: Machine learning is increasingly used to explore structure-property relationships in dendrimer-drug systems; however, its integration with topology-based structural compatibility analysis remains limited. This study presents a learning-driven framework to evaluate the topology-based structural compatibility of perylene diimide core dendrimers with antiviral, antioxidant, and imaging agents. Within a quantitative structure-property relationship framework, linear regression, Gaussian process regression (GPR), and artificial neural networks are employed to identify dominant graph-theoretic topological indices and to capture linear and nonlinear structure-property relationships. These insights are combined with a structure-based compatibility analysis that ranks dendrimer generations without altering drug identity or ordering. Generation-wise compatibility is computed using standardized Euclidean distance after global normalization, and ranking stability is assessed through monotonic and magnitude analysis. Results show class-dependent descriptor relevance, with GPR achieving test-set R 2 values above 0.94 for molecular weight, exact mass, monoisotopic mass, and heavy atom count. The generation-wise compatibility analysis further reveals distinct topology-based structural compatibility patterns across the investigated drug classes, highlighting the value of integrating machine learning with graph-theoretic analysis for rational nanocarrier design and the computational assessment of potential encapsulation suitability.

items.title: Probing Genomic Foundation Models with Splice-Variant Perturbations
items.abstract_or_text: As benchmarks saturate, traditional validation methods fail to capture the probabilistic representations of genomic foundation models. This study probes self-supervised generalists (NTv3 650M, Evo2 40B, Genos 10B) alongside task-specific specialists (SpliceAI, AlphaGenome, Borzoi) using a mechanistically focused paradigm centered on expert-curated single-nucleotide substitutions within the splicing regions of the exon-rich OPA1 gene. Extending this analysis across the broader corpus of OPA1 mutations, variants of uncertain significance (VUS), and an independent 65-gene dataset of spliceogenic mutations demonstrates that foundation models not only match task-specific networks, but also generalize across mutation types. Training data scale, genetic diversity, and evolutionary context are key for capturing RNA splicing syntax, whereas sparse routing may constrain performance. Mechanistically, foundation models exhibit a compute asymmetry: Evo2 40B frontloads compute into massive parameter scale to resolve single-nucleotide variants within a narrow 425-bp context window, whereas the bidirectional NTv3 650M model and the Genos 10B mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture backload compute to inference, requiring spatial logit aggregation and vast context windows of up to 94 kb. Furthermore, accuracy may benefit from locus-specific thresholding rather than mutation-class calibration, exposing representation boundaries of the self-supervised models.

items.title: SMFnet reveals principles of combinatorial transcription factor assembly
items.abstract_or_text: Combinatorial assembly of transcription factors (TFs) opens chromatin at cis-regulatory elements (cREs) to establish cell-type-specific gene expression. Dissecting the role of individual TFs and their collective function has been limited by the diversity of TF binding-site arrangements across cREs. A single regulatory sequence can support multiple configurations of TF and nucleosome occupancy, raising the possibility that distinct chromatin states reflect different TF assemblies. Predictive models linking regulatory sequence to chromatin accessibility collapse these distinct molecular states into population averages, obscuring how TF assemblies shape accessible chromatin. Here, we introduce SMFNet, a generative diffusion model that predicts distributions of single-molecule chromatin accessibility profiles from DNA sequence, and PRISM, which identifies sequence features associated with individual molecular states. Together, these approaches enable us to systematically associate single molecule chromatin states at cREs with specific TF binding motifs. Experimental perturbation of these motifs redistributes the corresponding states as predicted by SMFNet, supporting their interpretation as TF-dependent configurations underlying chromatin opening. We then use controlled in silico motif screens to systematically dissect individual and combinatorial TF contributions to chromatin opening. Individual TFs show distinct chromatin-opening signatures, differing in accessible-region width and nucleosome-positioning precision even when associated with similar levels of chromatin accessibility. Combining motifs reveals partner- and spacing-dependent effects on chromatin accessibility, TF occupancy and nucleosome positioning. Genetic perturbation of TF binding sites using natural variation at endogenous cRE confirms that TF-specific properties shape chromatin accessibility in vivo. Together, our findings reveal sequence-encoded principles of combinatorial TF assembly during chromatin opening.

items.title: Cannabidiol Impairs Glucagon Trafficking and Secretion Through the Lysosomal System in Murine αTC1-6 cells
items.abstract_or_text: Glucagon secretion by pancreatic cells is regulated by nutrient, paracrine, and neural inputs, and emerging evidence suggests that the islet endocannabinoid system (ECS) may also regulate -cell function. While phytocannabinoids such as cannabidiol (CBD) have been shown to interact with the ECS, and negatively regulate insulin secretion from pancreatic {beta} cells, whether CBD alters cell function in ways that disrupt glucagon trafficking and secretion remains unclear. This study investigates how acute CBD exposure affects transcriptional and secretory networks governing cell function. Using the TC1-6 glucagon-secreting cell line, we exposed the cells to 0.3 and 3 M CBD for RT-qPCR analysis, 3 M CBD for bulk RNA sequencing, and 3 M CBD or its inactive metabolite 7-COOH-CBD for imaging and secretion experiments. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that treatment with CBD did not alter the expression of ECS receptors and enzymes. However, pathways involved in cellular excitability, peptide hormone trafficking, and secretion were significantly downregulated. Using confocal microscopy, we found that CBD exposure increased the colocalization of glucagon with LAMP1 (a lysosomal marker), and that CBD rerouted peripheral glucagon, and glucagon-containing lysosomes towards the intracellular region of the cell. In conjunction with these findings, we observed reduced glucose-stimulated glucagon secretion under high glucose conditions. Overall, our data supports a model in which acute CBD exposure downregulates processes governing cellular excitability and peptide secretion and negatively regulates glucagon trafficking and secretion by rerouting peripheral glucagon into lysosome-associated intracellular compartments in TC1-6 cells.

items.title: The Quagmire of Immunogenicity-Guided Antibody Design: Labels Limit Progress
items.abstract_or_text: Generative sequence-based antibody design is increasingly steered by learned property predictors, so a design objective is only as well specified as the labels behind its oracle. Immunogenicity is among the most clinically consequential properties to condition on, and among the least well specified: the supervisory signal is a single anti-drug-antibody percentage (ADA%) per molecule, aggregated from published trials. To analyze that signal, we first extended and corrected the widely used 217-entry dataset to 231 therapeutics with paired sequences, spanning formats from mouse to fully human. Then, we manually reconstructed the clinical evidence for 110 of them from primary sources. We find that an antibody format lookup outperforms every sequence-based learned predictor on the 231-antibody dataset. Apparent accuracy tracks the format composition of the evaluation split rather than sequence signal. Furthermore, the labels understate their own evidence: molecules labeled at [≤]6 ADA% span up to 86% across trials. We recomputed labels from the trial-level measurements and found that the advantage of the format-based approach disappears, while the sequence-based predictors degrade less under the cohort-weighted mean. We conclude that progress is limited by the label itself, and recommend reporting ADA% at the trial level, treating the target as a distribution rather than a point value, and evaluating against a format-based baseline.

items.title: Differentiable Spin-Center Diffusion Model Enables DEER-Guided Generative Pipeline of Weighted Protein Ensembles
items.abstract_or_text: Biological function entails the interconversion of a protein between distinct conformations, an equilibrium modulated by ligands and other physicochemical conditions. Double electron-electron resonance (DEER) spectroscopy captures these ensembles as distance distributions, P(r), between spin label pairs. However, the width of P(r) convolves protein conformational heterogeneity with the rotameric flexibility of the label. Because current spin label models overestimate this contribution, translating P(r) into ensembles has remained indirect and predominantly qualitative. Here, we developed spin-center (SC) diffusion, a differentiable model of the spin label with a tunable spin label rotameric width. Coupled to a frozen Boltz-2 structure generator, SC diffusion enables the entire experimental P(r) to guide ensemble generation at inference time. We demonstrate the robustness of this pipeline on synthetic P(r) of known composition, recovering the ensemble populations, including both components of a bimodal profile. Guided by experimental P(r) measured under different biochemical conditions, ensembles of the transporters PfMATE, LmrP, MhsT and P-glycoprotein were modeled and free energy differences derived from the ensembles in a condition-dependent manner. By embedding a differentiable label model in structure generation, our approach interprets DEER distributions as weighted conformational ensembles, adding a missing thermodynamic grounding to generative protein structure prediction methods.

items.title: Ultra-rare coding variants in schizophrenia risk genes are associated with longitudinal phenotypic differences across psychotic disorders
items.abstract_or_text: Background: The Schizophrenia Exome Meta-Analysis (SCHEMA) Consortium has recently identified 40 genes at a false discovery rate <0.05 in which ultra-rare damaging variants substantially increase schizophrenia (SZ) risk. However, the impact of these variants on clinical trajectories across the psychosis spectrum is not yet known. Methods: We screened 9,821 sequenced participants with psychotic disorders who passed genomic quality control from the SUPER-Finland psychosis study for ultra-rare variants predicted to be damaging in these 40 SZ-associated genes, identifying 163 variant carriers. To assess the impact of these variants on clinical course and functioning across psychotic disorders, we used five decades of nationwide, full-coverage health register data together with interview, questionnaire, and cognitive assessments collected at study enrollment. We compared the clinical trajectories and functional outcomes of these variant carriers with those of non-carriers, including comparisons across different strata of the schizophrenia polygenic risk score (SZ-PGS) and with participants harboring deleterious variants in other genes associated with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Results: Overall, the variant carriers had a similar distribution of major psychotic disorder diagnoses to that of non-carriers. Despite this diagnostic similarity, variant carriers had earlier hospital admissions than non-carriers for both psychiatric (HR=2.30 [1.48-3.57], p=2.05e-04) and non-psychiatric diagnoses (HR=1.40 [1.10-1.79], p=6.88e-03), indicating increased medical needs early in life. They also showed greater exposure to childhood adversity, lower attainment of adult social milestones, and poorer neuropsychological test performance at study inclusion. Across longitudinal measures, variant carriers showed less favorable clinical and functional trajectories than non-carriers and clustered more closely with individuals with high SZ-PGS ([≥]90th percentile). Consistent with a liability-threshold model, the variant carriers had lower SZ-PGS than non-carriers among participants with a diagnosis of SZ ({beta} = -0.40, p = 5.32e-05) but higher SZ-PGS than population controls ({beta} = 0.55, p = 9.36e-08), suggesting that the variant carriers developed psychosis at lower levels of common-variant liability. Gene-level analyses identified associations of variants in AKAP11, SETD1A, and XPO7 with lower SZ-PGS and/or poorer neuropsychological test performance, while carriers of damaging variants in SZ-risk genes also associated with bipolar disorder showed high cumulative burdens of affective disorder diagnoses. Conclusion: The disease trajectories of carriers of ultra-rare damaging variants in SZ-risk genes broadly overlapped with those of non-carriers, but carriers showed several differences: greater childhood adversity, earlier hospitalizations, and poorer neuropsychological test performance. These carrier-associated differences were detectable across psychotic disorder diagnoses and suggest a broader phenotypic impact of rare SZ-risk variants than is captured by SZ diagnosis alone, with potential clinical relevance for future risk stratification and genetic counseling.

items.title: Acute Communicating Hydrocephalus Caused by a Lumbar Intraneural Cavernous Hemangioma in a Child: A Case Report
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Hydrocephalus secondary to a spinal lesion is rare and exceptional in children. Intraneural hemangiomas of the spinal nerve roots typically present with radicular symptoms; their association with hydrocephalus has been reported almost exclusively in adults. We report a previously healthy 5-year-old boy who presented with acute communicating hydrocephalus requiring emergency external ventricular drainage. Cerebrospinal fluid protein was markedly elevated without a cellular reaction, and no intracranial cause was identified. Spinal magnetic resonance imaging revealed an intradural mass at L3–L4 within the filum terminale fibers; resection yielded complete resolution of the hydrocephalus, and histopathology confirmed an intraneural cavernous hemangioma. At 6-year follow-up the child remained well, with no recurrence. To our knowledge, this is the youngest reported case of an intraneural hemangioma of the spinal nerve roots, and the first in any age group in which this lesion presented with acute communicating hydrocephalus. Spinal pathology should be considered in unexplained pediatric communicating hydrocephalus with elevated CSF protein; definitive resection can resolve the hydrocephalus and avoid permanent shunting.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy, Self-Perceived Competence, and Use Among Postgraduate Medical Trainees and Faculty in Tanzania: A Multi-Institutional Cross-Sectional Study
items.abstract_or_text: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is being integrated into medical education globally, yet evidence from sub-Saharan Africa remains sparse. Postgraduate medical training institutions in this region face distinctive cultural, resource and infrastructure constraints that may shape how educators and trainees engage with AI. This study examined knowledge and self-reported use of AI among postgraduate medical residents and faculty in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted across three postgraduate medical training universities in Dar es Salaam the Aga Khan University (AKU), Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (MUHAS), and Hubert Kairuki Memorial University (HKMU). A census sampling approach was used, targeting all available residents and faculty. Data was collected via an online structured questionnaire assessing AI knowledge, exposure, and self-rated competence. Knowledge scores were derived from a ten-item questionnaire and compared across groups using Welch's t-test and multivariable linear regression to determine association with knowledge scores. Results A total of 155 participants participated in the study (116 residents, 39 faculty). Mean age group was 31–40 years. Formal AI training was rare (7.1%), yet 80.0% reported using AI in teaching or learning activities. Residents used AI substantially more than faculty (65.8% vs. 14.2%). Overall objective knowledge was moderate (mean score 59.0%, SD 18.2%), with no significant difference between residents and faculty (p = 0.623). Specialty was also associated with knowledge scores, with medical and radiology specialties outperforming non-clinical specialties Self-rated knowledge at Level 5 was the only independent predictor of higher objective scores in multivariable analysis (β = 0.151; 95% CI 0.022–0.302; p = 0.049). Conclusions AI use is widespread among postgraduate trainees in Dar es Salaam despite minimal formal training. Knowledge gaps are evident, particularly around foundational AI concepts. Self-perceived competence, rather than professional role or formal training, predicted objective knowledge. These findings underscore the need for structured, contextually adapted AI literacy curricula within postgraduate medical education in Tanzania and similar settings.

items.title: Copper-Mediated Radiofluorination of the Excitatory Amino Acid Transporter 2 (EAAT2)-Targeted PET Tracer [ 18 F]RP-115: Alternate Synthetic Method.
items.abstract_or_text: Excitatory amino acid transporter 2 (EAAT2) is a key regulator of extracellular glutamate in the central nervous system. Dysregulated EAAT2 is implicated in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease (AD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), highlighting EAAT2 as a potential target for PET imaging. We previously reported a multistep radiosynthesis of [ 18 F]RP-115, a CNS-permeable prodrug that undergoes esterase-mediated hydrolysis in the CNS to yield the active EAAT2-binding carboxylate. Motivated by recent advances in copper-mediated radiofluorination (CMRF), we sought to develop a more efficient late-stage radiosynthesis of [ 18 F]RP-115. A two-step radiosynthesis of [ 18 F]RP-115 using CMRF provided [ 18 F]RP-115 in high radiochemical yield (52.8% ± 2.1 %, decay-corrected from starting [ 18 F]fluoride ion, n = 4), high molar activity (355 ± 61 GBq/μmol), and high radiochemical purity (> 99%) with a total synthesis time of 70 min. Chiral HPLC analysis demonstrated that the configuration of the aspartic acid residue remained intact without racemization during both the CMRF and trifluoroacetic acid mediated deprotection. We developed an efficient radiosynthesis of [ 18 F]RP-115 via CMRF, achieving high radiochemical yield and molar activity. This efficient synthesis may serve as a basis for the future implementation of a CMRF-based automated radiosynthesis of [ 18 F]RP-115.

items.title: Glial Dysfunction and Memory Impairments in a Model of Pediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
items.abstract_or_text: Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (POSA) is a common childhood disease that often causes aberrant brain development and cognitive deficits. The pathophysiological underpinnings of cognitive impairments in POSA remain unclear. Here, we examined cellular and molecular aspects of pathology in a mouse model of POSA that features learning and memory deficits. We performed single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) of the hippocampus to examine gene expression changes in an unbiased and cell type-specific manner. This dataset revealed a striking perturbation of transcriptomes across all brain cell types, particularly within glia and neural stem cells. We validated reduced expression of several differentially expressed genes at protein level: QDPR and SOX8 in oligodendrocytes, LRRK2 and NDUFS4 in neural stem cells, TFE3 in microglia, and GLUT1 in astrocytes. Comparison of oligodendrocyte gene expression changes with proteomic datasets suggested impairments in myelination, which we confirmed in vivo. Furthermore, cellular level analyses demonstrated aberrant morphology of oligodendrocytes, astrocytes, and microglia in the hippocampus, and diminished numbers of neural stem cells in the subgranular zone. Our study identifies cellular and molecular glial cell dysfunction in POSA, validates gene targets for further study, and provides an snRNA-seq dataset to facilitate further data-driven hypothesis generation.

items.title: Glutamine antagonism suppresses tumor growth in adrenocortical carcinoma through inhibition of de novo nucleotide biosynthesis
items.abstract_or_text: Dysregulation of cellular metabolism is a hallmark of cancer, which remains poorly understood in adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC). Here, we dissected ACC metabolism by integrating transcriptional profiling from human and mouse ACC, targeted tissue metabolomics from a mouse ACC model, and untargeted serum metabolomics from a large patient cohort, providing cross-species validation of metabolic rewiring in ACC. This study revealed global metabolic dysregulation, involving glutamine-dependent pathways such as amino-acid and hexosamine biosynthesis, nucleotide metabolism, and glutathione biosynthesis, suggesting glutamine catabolism is a critical metabolic vulnerability in ACC. Treatment with glutamine antagonists 6-Diazo-5-Oxo-L-Norleucine (DON) and JHU-083 elicited robust anti-tumor responses. Mechanistic studies revealed DON's anti-tumor effect was primarily driven by selective inhibition of glutamine-fueled de novo nucleotide biosynthesis. Additionally, DON led to DNA damage, which yielded potent synergism with inhibition of the DNA damage response pathway. Collectively, this work highlights glutamine metabolism as a central metabolic dependency and therapeutic target in ACC.

items.title: Digital pathological classification of peripheral neuroblastic tumors across multi-continent cohorts
items.abstract_or_text: Peripheral neuroblastic tumors (pNTs) are embryonal tumors of neural crest origin with highly variable clinical behaviors, ranging from spontaneous regression to aggressive and fatal disease. The International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification (INPC) defines four diagnostic categories and stratifies tumors into Favorable Histology (FH) or Unfavorable Histology (UH) group based on age-linked assessment of tumor differentiation/maturation and the Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index (MKI). Prognostic distinction according to INPC offers significant prediction of clinical outcomes, with patients harboring FH tumors demonstrating longer overall and event-free survival than those with UH tumor. Here, we assembled the largest multi-continental whole-slide histology imaging dataset of pNTs to date, comprising 2,030 tumors from the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Germany and Japan. Using this dataset, we developed NB-PathAssist, a computational pathology framework for automated INPC-based classification from digitized whole-slide images. NB-PathAssist integrates foundation-model-based feature extraction with an archetype-guided SummaryMixing architecture that compresses whole-slide morphology into representative histologic tokens for tumor-level classification. To automate MKI assessment, we manually annotated 14,049 nuclei, classifying them as mitotic-karyorrhectic (MK) tumor cells, non-MK tumor cells, or non-tumor cells. The resulting model was applied to phenotype cells in whole-slide images across 1,649 tissue sections. Across geographically and institutionally diverse cohorts, NB-PathAssist reproducibly assessed key diagnostic features and generated prognostic classifications concordant with reference INPC annotations. The average balanced accuracy for classifying tumor categories, grade of neuroblastic differentiation, MKI and prognostic groups achieved 0.84, 0.86, 0.89 and 0.96, respectively. We packaged the NB-PathAssist algorithms into an end-to-end online platform for scalable and standardized AI-assisted assessment of pNTs.

items.title: Regulatory plasticity of the rdar biofilm morphotype in clinical uropathogenic Escherichia coli and its modulation by ciprofloxacin
items.abstract_or_text: Background: Red, dry and rough (rdar) biofilm formation in Escherichia coli is characterized by the coordinated production of extracellular cellulose and amyloid curli fimbriae. Although rdar biofilm formation has been extensively characterized in laboratory strains, its clinical relevance and implications for antimicrobial treatment remain poorly understood. Methods: We screened 146 consecutive E. coli isolates from patients with urinary tract infections in Lahore, Pakistan (2017-2019) for Congo red morphotypes at 28 degrees C and 37 degrees C. Antimicrobial susceptibility was determined by disc diffusion and compared between morphotypes using the Fisher exact test. Fourteen isolates were whole-genome sequenced, the csgD-csgBA intergenic region was aligned, and csgD expression was quantified by qRT-PCR. The effect of 10 micrograms/mL ciprofloxacin on rdar morphotype expression, matrix ultrastructure and biofilm formation was examined in ciprofloxacin-resistant isolates (MIC at least 128 micrograms/mL). Results: Rdar-like colony morphotypes were expressed by 36.3% (53/146) of isolates at 28 degrees C and 29.5% (43/146) at 37 degrees C. Nucleotide polymorphisms in the csgD-csgBA intergenic region clustered within annotated OmpR, IHF and CsgD binding regions and were associated with, but did not individually predict, the mode of rdar morphotype expression. Isolates carrying the rdar morphotype were distributed across diverse E. coli phylogroups and sequence types. Resistance to aztreonam, cefuroxime and cephradine was more frequent among smooth and white isolates, whereas resistance to nitrofurantoin was more frequent among isolates rdar-positive at 28 degrees C (45.2% versus 20.2%, p = 0.0097); fluoroquinolone resistance did not differ between morphotypes. Subinhibitory ciprofloxacin (10 micrograms/mL) suppressed rdar biofilm formation, disrupted extracellular matrix architecture and abolished surface colonization on glass, in ciprofloxacin-resistant isolates. Conclusions: Our findings establish the rdar morphotype as a clinically relevant biofilm phenotype in uropathogenic E. coli and show that subinhibitory ciprofloxacin suppresses rdar biofilm formation in ciprofloxacin-resistant isolates. These results underscore the importance of considering antibiotic-mediated modulation of biofilm behavior when interpreting treatment responses and designing strategies to combat persistent urinary tract infections.

items.title: Fertilization offsets the maternal age effect on mouse oocytes provided the oviduct is not itself aged
items.abstract_or_text: Advanced maternal age compromises oocyte quality, and it is widely assumed that these deficits are transmitted to embryos. However, because most studies rely on in vivo conception, it has been difficult to separate the effects of oocyte aging from those of an aged fertilization environment. In aging mice, we observed that the fraction of ovulated oocytes forming implantation sites after in vivo conception fell ~3.7-fold, raising the question of whether this was due to reduced fertilization, reduced embryo quality or reduced support from the aged reproductive tract. Therefore we fertilized oocytes of aged and young mice in vitro with a shared young-donor sperm preparation, holding the fertilization environment constant and removing paternal variability. Hallmarks of maternal age were largely offset following fertilization in vitro: aged oocytes produced blastocysts at rates comparable to young controls, with altered - but not deficient - cell-lineage composition and no detectable impairment in development to term (E18.5) after transfer to young oviducts. Proteomic analysis revealed that, unlike the transcriptomic signature, the proteomic age signature of oocytes was not faithfully propagated to the blastocyst: for a subset of proteins, particularly those depleted in aged oocytes, the direction of the age effect reversed between oocyte and blastocyst. Comparison with parthenogenetically activated oocytes showed this divergence to be fertilization-dependent, implicating fertilization - rather than mere embryonic cleavage - as the driver of proteomic change. Stable-isotope labelling in live embryos showed that blastocysts from aged, fertilized oocytes both synthesized more new protein and retained less maternal protein than young counterparts; neither effect was detectable after parthenogenesis. Puromycin labelling, by contrast, showed a maternal-age-associated rise in bulk synthesis regardless of route. Together, these results indicate that the maternal-age effect on the oocyte proteome is labile rather than fixed and can be offset by fertilization itself, provided the maternal environment is not itself aged.

items.title: Variantscape: Retrospective Study of Large Language Model-Based Extraction of Variant-Treatment-Cancer Associations from Published Oncology Abstracts
items.abstract_or_text: Objectives: Precision oncology relies on accurate interpretation of tumour-detected gene variants, to guide personalised treatment decisions. However, interpretation of variants in context requires extensive information that is often buried within unstructured biomedical literature and obscured by inconsistent nomenclature, making manual retrieval labour-intensive and prone to omissions. In this study, our aim was to evaluate the potential of large language models to extract variant-treatment-cancer associations at scale from published abstracts. Design: We developed Variantscape, a large-scale, automated pipeline and open-access web tool. It integrates traditional natural language processing methods with state-of-the-art large language models to extract, standardise, and analyse co-associations between genetic variants, cancer types, and therapeutic interventions from published biomedical abstracts. Results: From over 3.7 million abstracts published between January 2014 and October 2026, 886,195 articles containing gene names were eligible for extraction. Among these, 37,895 (4.3%) mentioned a variant, cancer type, and therapeutic agent together, covering 11,985 unique variants across 197 cancer types and 547 therapeutic agents. LLM verification against the abstract text confirmed at least one association in 35,224 papers, giving a literature-derived graph of 10,571 nodes and 44,644 verified edges. Canonical alterations in well-studied cancers (e.g., BRAF V600E in melanoma) were strongly linked to established treatments, while several rare variants also emerged with high-confidence literature support. Conclusions: By applying large language models to biomedical literature, Variantscape enables scalable, context-aware extraction of trilateral variant-treatment-cancer relationships. This approach supports early evidence synthesis/hypothesis generation, highlights underrecognized or rare associations for MTB preparation, and offers a practical resource for accelerating discovery and supporting precision oncology research and translation.
